title: Transmission slipping
metaDesc: Engine revs but the car doesn't speed up? Answer a few questions to see if it's low fluid, worn parts or a sensor, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: revs high but car doesnt accelerate
engine revs but car wont go faster
rpm goes up but car doesnt speed up
car loses power and revs up
intro: A slipping transmission lets the engine rev up without the car speeding up to match, like spinning your wheels on ice. Slipping creates heat, and heat wears the transmission quickly, so catching it early matters. Answer a few questions to see the likely cause and how urgent it is.
safety: If the car loses drive and won't move or barely moves, get to the side of the road and have it towed.
If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
If a transmission temperature warning comes on, pull over when it's safe and let it cool before deciding what to do.
Avoid highways and fast traffic while the transmission is slipping. It may not respond when you need power.

q_severity.q: Which of these best describes it right now?

opts.a: The car barely moves or won't move in some gears
There's a burning smell, or red or pink fluid under the car
A transmission warning or temperature light is on
It slips now and then, but the car still drives

q_trans_type.q: Is your car an automatic or a manual (stick shift with a clutch pedal)?
q_trans_type.help: CVTs (continuously variable transmissions) count as automatics here. They don't have fixed gears, so slipping feels like the revs rising with little extra speed.

q_fluid.q: Have you been able to check the transmission fluid?
q_fluid.help: Many cars have a transmission dipstick, often with a yellow or red handle; others have none and must be checked by a shop. Your owner's manual explains how (usually engine running, warmed up, in Park on level ground). Healthy fluid is usually red or pink and doesn't smell burnt.

opts.a: The level is OK, but the fluid is dark brown or smells burnt
The level and color look normal
My car has no dipstick / I'm not sure
Mostly when cold, and it gets better as it warms up
Mostly when hot, after a long drive, towing or stop-and-go traffic
During one particular shift, like from 2nd to 3rd
At steady highway speed, the revs creep up without any gear change
Along with a check engine light

result.title: The transmission has lost most of its ability to drive the car
result.now: Don't try to force it by revving the engine. Put it in Park, turn it off and have the car towed.
if: If you're stuck in a lane, turn on your hazard lights and call for help from a safe place.
If there's red or pink fluid under the car, a leak may be the cause. Mention it when you call.
If you smell burning or see smoke, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
result.why: When the engine runs but the car barely moves, the transmission isn't holding. Revving it harder makes the slipping parts even hotter and can turn a repair into a full replacement.

causes.name: Very low fluid from a leak
causes.clues: Red or pink fluid under the car, or a recent bump or scrape underneath.

causes.name: Badly worn internal clutches or bands
causes.clues: High mileage and slipping that got worse over weeks.

causes.name: Failed pump or torque converter
causes.clues: A whining or grinding noise that changes with engine speed.

you: From outside the car, look for red or pink fluid underneath.

result.title: The transmission may be leaking fluid or overheating
result.now: Pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have the car towed.
if: If you see smoke, step away from the car. Fluid dripping on the exhaust can catch fire.
If the leak is only a few drops and there's no burning smell, still have it inspected before driving it. Note the color and size of the drips for the shop.
If there are flames, or the smoke keeps growing, move well away from the car and call 911.
result.why: Transmission fluid cools and lubricates the transmission and gives it the pressure to hold each gear. A leak lowers that pressure and causes slipping, and a burning smell means fluid or parts are overheating. Both cause fast, expensive wear.

causes.name: Leaking pan gasket, cooler line or seal
causes.clues: Red or pink fluid under the middle or front of the car.

causes.name: Overheating from slipping
causes.clues: A sharp burnt smell after driving, with no visible leak.

causes.name: Fluid dripping onto the hot exhaust
causes.clues: Smoke from under the car along with the leak.

you: Note the color of any fluid under the car. Red or pink usually means transmission fluid.

result.title: The transmission may be overheating or has detected a fault
result.now: Pull over when it's safe, put it in Park and let it cool. Then have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the light goes off after cooling, it still needs checking before you rely on it. Slipping and overheating feed each other.
If you smell burning or see smoke, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
If the engine temperature gauge is high too, don't restart the engine. Have it towed.
result.why: Transmission fluid breaks down quickly when it gets too hot, which leads to more slipping and more heat. A warning light plus slipping means the transmission is already protecting itself or warning you that damage is possible.

causes.name: Low fluid
causes.clues: A leak, or a level below the mark on the dipstick.

causes.name: Slipping clutches making heat
causes.clues: Slipping that started before the light came on.

causes.name: Blocked or damaged transmission cooler
causes.clues: It mostly happens when towing, in hot weather or in heavy traffic.

you: Once it's cool, check for leaks under the car.

result.title: On a manual, the clutch is the first thing to check
result.now: Have the clutch checked within the next few days. Until then, drive gently and avoid hard acceleration in high gears.
if: If the clutch pedal feels soft, sinks or stays down, don't rely on the car. You may not be able to shift or take it out of gear. Have it checked before driving further.
If you smell burning, pull over and let it cool. Slipping that bad can mean the clutch is close to failing, so have it checked before driving further.
If the car won't move in gear, or you can't get it into gear, have it towed.
result.why: A clutch grips the engine to the transmission. When it wears thin, or gets oil on it, it may not hold full power, so the revs jump without more speed. It's usually most noticeable in higher gears and going uphill.

causes.name: Worn clutch disc
causes.clues: High mileage, and the clutch engages near the top of the pedal travel.

causes.name: Oil or fluid on the clutch
causes.clues: An oil leak where the engine and transmission join.

causes.name: Clutch hydraulic problem
causes.clues: A soft, sinking or sticking clutch pedal, or low clutch fluid.

you: Notice where the clutch starts to grab. Very high on the pedal usually means wear.
Check the clutch fluid reservoir if your car has one.
shop: Inspection for oil leaks at the clutch

result.title: Low transmission fluid may be causing the slip, and a leak is likely
result.now: If your car has a dipstick, top up with the exact fluid type listed in your owner's manual, following its check procedure and not overfilling. Then have the leak found within the next few days. If you're unsure of the fluid type or procedure, let a shop do it.
if: If it still slips after topping up, avoid driving it until it's checked. Each slip adds heat and wear.
If the level drops again quickly, or you see drips, stop using the car until the leak is fixed.
If the car loses drive, you smell burning, see smoke, or a transmission warning light comes on, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: An automatic transmission uses fluid pressure to hold each gear. When the level is low, pressure drops and the clutches inside slip. Fluid doesn't get used up like fuel, so a low level usually means a leak.

causes.name: Leaking pan gasket or seal
causes.clues: Red or pink drips under the middle of the car.

causes.name: Leaking cooler line
causes.clues: Drips near the front of the car, under the radiator.

causes.name: Wrong level after a recent service
causes.clues: The problem started soon after a fluid change.

you: Check the level again after a few days of driving.
Put cardboard under the car overnight to spot drips.
shop: Correct fluid level check to factory procedure

result.title: Burnt-smelling fluid suggests the transmission has been running hot and may be worn inside
result.now: Have the transmission inspected within the next few days. Keep trips short and gentle until then.
if: If the slipping gets worse, you smell burning, or a warning light comes on, stop driving it and have it towed.
If the shop finds metal particles or a lot of debris in the pan, a bigger repair is more likely than a simple fluid change. Ask them to show you what they found.
result.why: Dark, burnt-smelling fluid has usually been overheated, often by the very slipping you're feeling. Overheated fluid protects poorly, so wear speeds up. A shop can tell from the fluid and pan whether a service may help or whether there's internal damage.

causes.name: Worn clutches inside the transmission
causes.clues: High mileage and slipping that's slowly getting worse.

causes.name: Overdue fluid service
causes.clues: No record of a fluid change, especially with towing or heavy use.

causes.name: Overheating from towing or a cooler problem
causes.clues: Slipping started after towing, mountain driving or hot weather.

you: Find your records of the last transmission fluid service.

result.title: Slipping only when cold can point to early wear or hardened internal seals
result.now: Let the car warm up for a minute or two before driving off, go easy until it's warm, and book a transmission check when convenient.
if: If it starts slipping when warm too, get it checked within a few days.
If the fluid level turns out to be low, top it up with the correct type and look for a leak.
If the car loses drive, you smell burning, see smoke, or a transmission warning light comes on, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: Cold fluid is thicker, and rubber seals inside the transmission shrink and harden with age. Worn seals can leak pressure when cold, so a gear doesn't fully grip until things warm up and expand. It tends to get worse over time, so it's worth having it looked at before it does.

causes.name: Hardened or worn internal seals
causes.clues: Older or high-mileage car, and the problem fades once warm.

causes.name: Slightly low fluid
causes.clues: A small leak, or a level at the low mark.

causes.name: Old or wrong-type fluid
causes.clues: No recent fluid service, or a recent service with a fluid not listed in the manual.

you: Note the outside temperature and how long it takes to go away.
shop: Line pressure test cold and warm

result.title: Slipping when hot can point to worn parts or fluid that's breaking down
result.now: Have the transmission checked within the next few days. Until then, avoid towing, long highway runs and heavy traffic when you can.
if: If a transmission temperature warning comes on, pull over and let it cool, then have it towed or checked by a mobile mechanic.
If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and have it towed.
If the car loses drive or the slipping gets suddenly worse, stop driving it and have it towed.
result.why: As fluid heats up it gets thinner, and worn parts that seal fine when cold start leaking pressure. Heat also breaks the fluid down further. Slipping when hot tends to make the transmission run even hotter, so it can get worse quickly.

causes.name: Worn internal clutches or seals
causes.clues: High mileage and slipping that's slowly getting worse.

causes.name: Worn or overheated fluid
causes.clues: Dark fluid, or no record of a fluid change.

causes.name: Transmission cooler blocked or not working
causes.clues: Worse in summer, when towing or in stop-and-go traffic.

you: Note how long you'd been driving and the outside temperature when it slipped.

result.title: Slipping on one shift is often traced to a shift solenoid or the clutch for that gear
result.now: Have the transmission checked within the next few days, and note exactly which shift slips so you can tell the shop.
if: If the check engine or transmission light comes on, have the codes read right away. They often name the solenoid involved.
If the car gets stuck in one gear, avoid highways and fast traffic and have it towed or checked as soon as you can.
If the car loses drive, you smell burning, see smoke, or a transmission warning light comes on, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: Each gear change is controlled by an electric solenoid that sends fluid to a set of clutches. If one solenoid sticks, or one clutch pack wears, you get slipping on that shift only while the others feel normal. A shop will usually test the solenoid and read live data before deciding whether the problem is electrical or inside the transmission.

causes.name: Sticking or failing shift solenoid
causes.clues: A check engine light, and the slip comes and goes.

causes.name: Worn clutch pack for that gear
causes.clues: The slip is always on the same shift and slowly getting worse.

causes.name: Valve body problem
causes.clues: Harsh or erratic shifts along with the slipping.

you: Write down which shift slips and at what speed.
shop: Road test with live transmission data

result.title: The torque converter's lockup may be slipping
result.now: Have it checked within the next few days. Keep highway trips short until then.
if: If you also feel a shudder like driving over rumble strips at steady speed, mention it. That's a common sign of a lockup problem.
If a check engine light comes on, have the code read. Lockup faults usually set a code.
If the car loses drive, you smell burning, see smoke, or a transmission warning light comes on, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: At cruising speed, an automatic locks the torque converter so the engine and transmission turn together. If that lockup clutch slips, or isn't being told to lock, the revs creep up a few hundred without any gear change and fuel economy drops.

causes.name: Worn torque converter lockup clutch
causes.clues: Revs creep up at steady speed, sometimes with a shudder.

causes.name: Faulty lockup solenoid
causes.clues: A check engine light, and the problem comes and goes.

causes.name: Worn or wrong fluid
causes.clues: Dark fluid, or a recent fluid change with a different type.

you: Watch the tachometer at a steady highway speed and note if the revs drift up.
shop: Road test watching converter slip data

result.title: An electronic fault may be causing the slipping. Get the codes read
result.now: Have the codes read within the next few days. Many parts stores read engine codes free, but transmission codes may need a shop scan tool.
if: If the car is stuck in one gear or feels very sluggish, it may be in a protective "limp" mode. Avoid highways and fast traffic, and get it checked right away.

A code points a shop toward a circuit or system, not always to a failed part. A shop will usually test the sensor, solenoid and wiring before replacing anything, and the fix may turn out simpler than a rebuild.
If the car loses drive, you smell burning, see smoke, or a transmission warning light comes on, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
result.why: Modern automatics are computer-controlled. A bad speed sensor, solenoid or wiring problem can make the transmission shift wrong or slip, and the computer usually stores a code. Reading it first avoids guessing.

causes.name: Faulty shift or pressure control solenoid
causes.clues: Codes about a solenoid or line pressure.

causes.name: Faulty speed sensor or wiring
causes.clues: The speedometer acts strangely, or shifts happen at odd times.

causes.name: Internal wear the computer detected
causes.clues: Codes about a gear ratio being wrong.

you: Have the codes read and write them down.

result.title: Have the transmission checked before the slipping gets worse
result.now: Book a transmission check within the next few days, and keep trips short and gentle until then.
if: If the car loses drive, you smell burning, see smoke, or a warning light comes on, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and have it towed.
If you can check the fluid and it's low, top it up with the correct type, then still have it checked. Low fluid usually means a leak.
result.why: Slipping almost never fixes itself, and each slip adds heat and wear. Catching it early gives you the best chance that a fluid service, solenoid or seal repair fixes it rather than a rebuild.

causes.name: Low or worn fluid
causes.clues: Drips under the car or no record of a fluid service.

causes.name: Solenoid or sensor fault
causes.clues: A check engine light or erratic shifting.

causes.name: Internal wear
causes.clues: High mileage and slipping that's gradually getting worse.

you: Look for red or pink drips where you park.
Note when it slips: cold or hot, which shift, what speed.
